name: Lumen Technologies

profile.reading: Lumen Technologies traces back to 1930 when F. E. Hogan Sr. sold the Oak Ridge Telephone Company, a 75 subscriber operation, and grew over the 20th century through the Century Telephone Enterprises name adopted in 1971 and a public listing in 1978. In the 21st century the company completed a series of large acquisitions: Qwest in a 12 billion dollar stock for stock merger completed April 1, 2011, Savvis, a cloud infrastructure and hosted IT provider, for 2 billion dollars in 2011, and Level 3 Communications in a 25 billion dollar deal that closed November 1, 2017. The company was known as CenturyLink through this period and renamed itself Lumen Technologies in September 2020. Critically for this registry entry, Wikipedia confirms that on May 2, 2017 CenturyLink sold its entire data center and colocation business to funds advised by BC Partners, together with Medina Capital Advisors and Longview Asset Management, for approximately 1.86 billion dollars, retaining only a 10 percent equity stake in the resulting company, Cyxtera Technologies. This means facilities carrying the Lumen or CenturyLink data center legacy, including this registry row, are very likely now Cyxtera facilities rather than current Lumen Technologies operations, though this specific building individual post 2017 ownership was not confirmed this session. Lumen Technologies is headquartered in Monroe, Louisiana. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.
profile.research_note: Strong divestiture signal: Wikipedia confirms CenturyLink/Lumen sold its entire data center and colocation business to Cyxtera Technologies in a May 2, 2017 transaction (approximately 1.86 billion dollars, BC Partners/Medina Capital/Longview Asset Management, Lumen retained 10 percent equity). This registry separately lists a Cyxtera operator record (3 facilities), suggesting these two operator entries may represent the same underlying facility lineage split inconsistently. profile.reading: Lumen Technologies traces back to 1930 when F. E. Hogan Sr. sold the Oak Ridge Telephone Company, a 75 subscriber operation, and grew over the 20th century through the Century Telephone Enterprises name adopted in 1971 and a public listing in 1978. In the 21st century the company completed a series of large acquisitions: Qwest in a 12 billion dollar stock for stock merger completed April 1, 2011, Savvis, a cloud infrastructure and hosted IT provider, for 2 billion dollars in 2011, and Level 3 Communications in a 25 billion dollar deal that closed November 1, 2017. The company was known as CenturyLink through this period and renamed itself Lumen Technologies in September 2020. Critically for this registry entry, Wikipedia confirms that on May 2, 2017 CenturyLink sold its entire data center and colocation business to funds advised by BC Partners, together with Medina Capital Advisors and Longview Asset Management, for approximately 1.86 billion dollars, retaining only a 10 percent equity stake in the resulting company, Cyxtera Technologies. This means facilities carrying the Lumen or CenturyLink data center legacy, including this registry row, are very likely now Cyxtera facilities rather than current Lumen Technologies operations, though this specific building individual post 2017 ownership was not confirmed this session. Lumen Technologies is headquartered in Monroe, Louisiana. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading:
Lumen Technologies is a public company trading as LUMN, SEC filer CIK 0000018926, headquartered in Denver, Colorado. The company was previously known as CenturyLink and absorbed Level 3 Communications after CenturyLink acquired it in 2017, before adopting the Lumen name.

Lumen's own about page describes the company as a global communications services provider built around a global fiber network, citing service-level figures such as wavelengths up to 400 gigabits per second and dedicated internet access up to 100 gigabits per second, but the fetched page did not state a company-wide data center count or capacity total. Recent 2026 trade press reports Lumen selling its Broomfield, Colorado office campus for $15 million, a former secondary office location rather than its current Denver headquarters.

The registry here tracks 19 Lumen facilities across twelve states, Arizona, California, Maryland, Minnesota, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington, and Wisconsin. Unlike the colocation REITs and hyperscalers elsewhere in this registry, Lumen's data centers function primarily as network edge and interconnection points supporting its fiber and telecommunications business, rather than as the company's core commercial product, so its facility footprint should be read as a distributed network-edge presence rather than a wholesale colocation portfolio comparable to Digital Realty's or Equinix's.
